analyst_view.overall: Early view: Barcelona host Celta between Atlético (2 December) and Manchester City (8 December), so Flick is likely to rotate, though they scored six against Alavés in their last home league game. Celta play at Marseille in the Europa League four days later, have the league's lowest-scoring games (10 for, 10 against) and a long injury list that Giráldez hopes to clear by late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Celta have conceded only 10 in 12 and their games average under two goals, and Barça are likely to rotate before Manchester City. I still expect Barça to win comfortably but lean lower, around 3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Barcelona's home game with Alavés had only 6 corners despite 77% possession, and Barça took just 2 at the Metropolitano; they score from inside the box rather than forcing corners. I lean lower, around 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Celta commit few fouls (8 against Levante, one yellow) and Barça's home win over Alavés had five bookings; nothing in the news moves me off about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots. Barça took only 13 shots in the 6-1 against Alavés because they scored so efficiently, and a rotated side before Manchester City may manage the game rather than chase volume. I lean lower, around 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10 on target, mostly Barça's. Barça are clinical at home (six goals from 13 shots against Alavés), so even with fewer shots the on-target count should hold up; I stay around 9-10.
